sar.narrative: On December 19, 2016, at 22:08:56, an online transaction of $55.68 was processed using a Visa credit card associated with customer C13171. The customer subsequently contacted the financial institution to dispute the purchase, explicitly stating that they did not authorize or make the transaction. The transaction was initiated over the internet using an unrecognized desktop device running the Chrome web browser and linked to a Hotmail email domain. Further analysis revealed that this desktop device was newly introduced to the account and had been utilized across four distinct customer accounts and four separate payment cards. The flagged activity coincided with a notable transaction velocity on the card, comprising three transactions within a single hour and eight transactions within a twenty-four-hour window. Although the transaction amount of $55.68 aligns closely with the cardholder's historical spending average of $54.27, the cardholder confirmed the activity was completely unauthorized. The circumstances indicate potential card-not-present fraud where compromised payment credentials were used on a shared, unverified device endpoint. To mitigate further risk, the financial institution blocked card C13171-K2 and escalated the activity for suspicious activity reporting.
